EU CSRD SCOPE CHECKER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Do you have to report under the CSRD?

Enter headcount, turnover and company type. You get the result under the Omnibus thresholds and the original CSRD side by side, the first financial year, and what to do if you are only hit by customer data requests.

A first read written from the Directive without a live lookup. The Omnibus is being transposed country by country; confirm the current text and your Member State's law. Not legal advice.

Fill in the figures, then click Check scope.

Result


    

    
 

  


  

    
What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Covers: the CSRD size tests, the Omnibus thresholds, previously reporting companies and non-EU groups.
    • 
      
  • Gives: in scope or not under each reading, the first financial year, and the next steps including the voluntary VSME route.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: how your Member State has transposed the Omnibus, group consolidation and exemptions, how employees and turnover are counted exactly, sector rules, and any change after this page was written. Your auditor decides national law questions.
    • 
    

    
Also see the CBAM cost estimator, the EU green claims checker and the NIS2 scope checker.

  


  

    
Common questions

    
What is the CSRD?

    
The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (EU) 2022/2464 requires in-scope companies to publish audited sustainability information under the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS), including a double-materiality assessment.

    
Did the Omnibus remove most companies from scope?

    
The Omnibus package agreed in late 2025 narrows mandatory scope to companies with more than 1,000 employees and more than EUR 450M net turnover, and delays the later waves. How and when each Member State puts this into national law varies, so this tool shows the original and the Omnibus reading side by side.

    
What if I am out of scope?

    
Large customers, banks and investors may still ask you for data. The Commission's voluntary standard for smaller companies (VSME) is the format the Omnibus makes the ceiling on such requests, so preparing one data set saves answering each questionnaire from scratch.

    
Does it cover non-EU companies?

    
Yes in outline: non-EU groups are tested on EU turnover (more than EUR 450M) and an EU subsidiary or branch (more than EUR 200M turnover). Check both the group and the EU entity.

    
Is my data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent; a test in the code asserts there are no network calls.

We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record: nothing you enter is saved anywhere.

    
Everything runs in your browser. Your answers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (analysis_run, example_loaded, summary_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device, never with any of your data, and are switched off by Do Not Track.
